Section 1. Purpose and Application 1.1. These Academic Policies and Procedures for Undergraduate Programs of the autonomous organization of education Nazarbayev University (hereinafter “the Policies and Procedures”) establish the academic policies and procedural inst ructions for undergraduate programs of the autonomous organization of education Nazarbayev University (hereinafter “the University”). 1.2. These Policies and Procedures apply to all students enrolled in any undergraduate program at the University. Section 2. Terms / Definitions 2.1. The following terms, definitions, and abbreviations are used in these Policies and Procedures: 1) Academic calendar – a calendar of important teaching, learning and assessment dates and deadlines

as well as organizing, coordinating and monitoring academic processes. 4) Add deadline – the period at the beginning of each semester when students can sign up/register for courses until the deadline for adding courses. 5) Bursar's Department – a structural division of the University responsible for monitoring and controlling financial operations associated with payment of stipends, receipt of student fees, tuition fee, and student trips. 6) Cumulative Grade Point Average (hereinafter “CGPA”) or Grade Point Average (hereinafter “GPA”) – a calculation of the average of all the grades a student has obtained that contribute to their degree. The Academic Year and Academic calendar 3.2.1. Undergraduate programs operate on the basis

internal policies and regulations, and Handbooks. 3.2. The Academic Year and Academic calendar 3.2.1. Undergraduate programs operate on the basis of an academic year divided into three academic periods: Fall and Spring semesters, and a Summer term. 3.2.2. Academic year functions within the academic calendar that is devel oped in accordance with the Academic Calendar Guidelines. 3.2.3. An orientation period takes place for new students at the beginning of the semester/term in order to allow them to adapt to the University environme nt, academic expectations and program requirements. 3.3. Students are notified via email of the dates for the course registrat ion period prior to the event. 3.3.2. By registering for a course, students commit to complying with all course requirements, including the attendance policy and the examination procedure s chosen and announced by the course instructor. 3.3.3. Priority Registration. The University conducts online course registration on a priority basis. Students are permitted to add and drop courses during the Add and Drop periods, respectively. Dates for Add and Drop deadlines are published in the Academic Calendar. When a student drops a course during the Drop period, no record of the original course remains in the student’s transcript. 3.3.12. Withdrawing from a course. A student may withdraw from a course prior to the Withdrawal deadline as scheduled in the Academic Calendar.

A student is waitlisted when the course they have attempt ed to register for is full. The waitlist places the student in a queue. When a place in the course becomes available, the top student on the waitlist is then registe red in the course and notified by

the course becomes available, the top student on the waitlist is then registe red in the course and notified by email. Once the waitlist period ends, the student will have time to register for alternate courses before the end of the Add deadline. 3.4. Attendance 3.4.1. Students are expected to attend all classes in courses for which the y are registered at the University. 3.4.2.
